title: Naive Bayes
description: Probabilistic classifier based on Bayes' theorem with feature independence assumptions.
name: Naive Bayes
summary: Naive Bayes uses Bayes' Theorem with the 'naive' assumption of conditional independence between every pair of features given the value of the class variable to predict target probabilities.
use_when: Building quick text classification baselines, such as spam filters or sentiment analysis.
avoid_when: Features are highly correlated and accurate probability calibration is required.
pros: Extremely fast to train and predict, requiring only single passes over data.
Performs exceptionally well with high-dimensional text datasets.
Requires relatively small amounts of training data to estimate parameters.
cons: Assumes completely independent features, which is almost never true in practice.
Produces poorly calibrated probability outputs (tends to output 0 or 1).
Vulnerable to the zero-frequency problem if a category is missing in training.

key_hyperparams.name: alpha
key_hyperparams.note: Additive smoothing parameter (Laplace/Lidstone smoothing). Set to 0 for no smoothing.

quick_start:
from sklearn.naive_bayes import MultinomialNB
import numpy as np

X = np.random.randint(5, size=(100, 100))
y = np.random.randint(2, size=100)
clf = MultinomialNB().fit(X, y)
preds = clf.predict(X[:1])
